findings.quote: This license shall be for a period of eleven (11) months commencing from the Commencement Date and ending on 31st August, 2027 (both days inclusive), unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Agreement.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: This clause specifies that your license to use the premises will last for 11 months, from October 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027. Be aware of this fixed period and plan your stay accordingly.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: Your license to use the premises is for a fixed period of 11 months, ending on August 31, 2027. You must vacate the premises by this date unless a new agreement is made to renew the license.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause clearly defines the license period as 11 months, ending on August 31, 2027. This provides a clear end date for the agreement, after which you will regain possession unless a new agreement is signed.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: The license agreement with your tenant is for a fixed term of 11 months and will automatically expire on August 31, 2027. Ensure the tenant vacates by this date or negotiate a new agreement if you wish to renew.

findings.quote: The Parties may, by mutual consent recorded in writing, renew this license for a further period on such terms, including a revised License Fee, as may be agreed between them at that time. Any such renewal shall be by a fresh agreement, which shall be duly stamped and registered.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: If you wish to continue living in the premises after 11 months, you will need to negotiate a new agreement with the landlord. The terms, including the rent, can be revised at that time, and a new agreement must be signed and registered.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: If you want to extend your stay beyond August 31, 2027, you must proactively discuss and agree upon a new license agreement with the landlord. Be prepared for potential changes in terms, including a revised monthly fee.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause allows for renewal by mutual consent and requires a fresh, duly stamped, and registered agreement. This ensures you can renegotiate terms, including the license fee, if you wish to continue the arrangement after the initial 11 months.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: If your tenant wishes to continue their stay after the initial 11 months, you will need to draft and register a completely new agreement. This gives you the opportunity to revise the monthly fee and other terms as you see fit.

findings.quote: The Licensee shall pay to the Licensor a monthly License Fee of Rs. 32,000/- (Rupees Thirty-Two Thousand only) for the use of the Licensed Premises.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: You will be required to pay a monthly license fee of Rs. 32,000/- for using the premises. Make sure this amount is within your budget.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: You are obligated to pay a monthly license fee of Rs. 32,000/- to the landlord. Ensure this payment is made consistently as per the agreement.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: You will receive a monthly license fee of Rs. 32,000/- from the tenant for the use of your property. Confirm this amount aligns with your expectations.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You are entitled to receive a monthly license fee of Rs. 32,000/- from the tenant. Track these payments to ensure they are received on time each month.

findings.quote: The License Fee shall be payable in advance on or before the 5th day of each English calendar month by bank transfer to the account designated by the Licensor in writing.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: You must pay the monthly license fee in advance on or before the 5th day of each month. Failure to do so could result in penalties.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: Remember to pay your monthly license fee by bank transfer on or before the 5th day of each month. Late payments will incur penalties as per the agreement.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: The monthly license fee is due in advance on or before the 5th day of each month. This provides a consistent payment schedule for your income.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: The tenant is required to pay the monthly license fee by the 5th of each month. Monitor your bank account to ensure timely receipt and follow up immediately if a payment is missed.

findings.quote: If any License Fee or other amount payable by the Licensee is not paid on its due date, the Licensee shall pay interest on the outstanding amount at the rate of twenty-four percent (24%) per annum from the due date until the date of actual payment, together with a late payment charge of Rs. 500/- (Rupees Five Hundred only) for every day of delay.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: Be aware that late payments for the license fee or any other amount will incur a high interest rate of 24% per annum, plus a daily late payment charge of Rs. 500. This can add up very quickly.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: If you fail to pay your license fee or any other amount on time, you will face a significant penalty: 24% annual interest on the overdue amount and a Rs. 500 daily late payment charge. Prioritise timely payments to avoid these steep costs.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause provides for substantial penalties for late payments: 24% annual interest and a daily late fee of Rs. 500. This incentivises the tenant to pay on time and provides you with compensation for delays.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You are entitled to charge 24% annual interest and a Rs. 500 daily late fee if the tenant does not pay the license fee or other amounts on time. Ensure you apply these penalties consistently if payments are delayed.

findings.quote: In addition to the License Fee, the Licensee shall bear and pay the monthly maintenance charges of the Society, together with all special levies, sinking fund contributions, repair fund contributions and non-occupancy charges levied by the Society in respect of the Licensed Premises during the License Period.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: Besides the monthly license fee, you will be responsible for paying the society's monthly maintenance charges, as well as any special levies, sinking fund, repair fund contributions, and non-occupancy charges. Factor these additional costs into your budget.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: You are responsible for paying the society's monthly maintenance charges, special levies, sinking fund contributions, repair fund contributions, and non-occupancy charges. Make sure you receive and pay these bills promptly, in addition to your license fee.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause shifts the burden of society maintenance charges and various other contributions and levies to the licensee. This is beneficial for you as it reduces your recurring expenses related to the property during the license period.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: The tenant is responsible for paying all society charges, including maintenance, special levies, sinking fund, repair fund contributions, and non-occupancy charges. You should ensure these are paid by the tenant to avoid any defaults with the society.

findings.quote: The Licensee shall pay the electricity charges as per the bills of the electricity supply company, the piped gas charges, and the charges for internet and cable television directly to the concerned service providers, and shall produce the paid receipts to the Licensor on demand.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: You are responsible for paying electricity, piped gas, internet, and cable television bills directly. You must also keep the payment receipts and provide them to the landlord if requested.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: You must pay electricity, piped gas, internet, and cable television bills directly to the service providers. Keep all paid receipts readily available, as the landlord may ask to see them.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause specifies that the tenant will directly pay for electricity, piped gas, internet, and cable television. This frees you from managing these utility payments and ensures the tenant is responsible for their consumption.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: The tenant is obligated to pay utility bills directly and show you the receipts upon request. Periodically check with the tenant for these receipts to ensure timely payments and prevent service disruptions.

findings.quote: The municipal property tax in respect of the Licensed Premises shall be borne and paid by the Licensor.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: The municipal property tax for the premises will be paid by the landlord, so this is not an expense you need to worry about.
lensExplanations.tenant_already_signed: You are not responsible for paying the municipal property tax; the landlord will handle this. This is an advantage for you.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: You will be responsible for paying the municipal property tax for the premises. Make sure to budget for this ongoing expense.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You are obligated to pay the municipal property tax for the licensed premises. Ensure you pay these taxes on time to avoid any penalties or issues with the municipal authorities.

findings.quote: The Licensee has, on or before the execution of this Agreement, paid to the Licensor an interest-free refundable Security Deposit of Rs. 1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand only) by bank transfer, the receipt whereof the Licensor hereby admits and acknowledges.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: You are required to pay an interest-free security deposit of Rs. 1,50,000/- to the landlord. Ensure this payment is properly documented and acknowledged before signing the agreement.

lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You have received an interest-free security deposit of Rs. 1,50,000/- from the tenant. This amount will be held until the tenant vacates and can be used to cover permitted deductions.

findings.quote: The Security Deposit shall be refunded to the Licensee within a reasonable time after the Licensee has handed over vacant and peaceful possession of the Licensed Premises to the Licensor, subject to the deductions permitted under this Clause 5.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: The security deposit will be refunded within a 'reasonable time' after you vacate the premises, subject to deductions. 'Reasonable time' is vague and could lead to disputes; you might want to negotiate a specific timeframe.

lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: You are obligated to refund the security deposit within a 'reasonable time' after the tenant vacates, minus any permitted deductions. The vagueness of 'reasonable time' gives you flexibility but could be a point of contention with the tenant.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You must refund the security deposit within a 'reasonable time' after the tenant vacates the premises, after making any necessary deductions. Ensure you process this refund promptly to avoid disputes, keeping in mind the ambiguity of 'reasonable time'.

findings.quote: The Licensor shall be entitled to deduct from the Security Deposit such amounts as the Licensor may, in his sole discretion, consider necessary towards unpaid dues, damage to the Licensed Premises or its contents, cleaning, and any other expenses incurred by the Licensor on account of the Licensee.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: The landlord has broad discretion to deduct amounts from your security deposit for unpaid dues, damages, cleaning, or 'any other expenses' incurred due to you. lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause gives you broad discretion to deduct from the security deposit for various reasons, including unpaid dues, damages, cleaning, and other expenses incurred because of the tenant. This offers significant protection for your property.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You have the right to deduct from the security deposit for unpaid dues, damages, cleaning, and other expenses, using your sole discretion. Ensure you clearly document the reasons for any deductions made.

findings.quote: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Agreement, a sum equal to one (1) month's License Fee shall in all cases be retained by the Licensor from the Security Deposit towards repainting of the Licensed Premises, irrespective of the condition in which the Licensed Premises are handed back.

findings.quote: If the amounts due from the Licensee exceed the Security Deposit, the Licensee shall pay the shortfall to the Licensor within seven (7) days of a written demand.

findings.quote: The Licensee agrees that the first eight (8) months of the License Period, that is, from 1st October, 2026 to 31st May, 2027, shall be a lock-in period during which the Licensee shall not terminate this Agreement or vacate the Licensed Premises.

lensExplanations.tenant_about_to_sign: You are bound to stay in the premises for the first eight months (October 1, 2026, to May 31, 2027). If your plans are uncertain, be aware that you cannot terminate the agreement or vacate during this period without facing a penalty.

This means the tenant cannot terminate the agreement or vacate the premises before this date without facing penalties, providing you with assured rental income for this duration.

findings.quote: If the Licensee terminates this Agreement or vacates the Licensed Premises for any reason before the expiry of the lock-in period, the Licensee shall be liable to pay to the Licensor the License Fee for the entire unexpired portion of the lock-in period, and the Licensor shall be entitled to recover such amount from the Security Deposit.

For example, if you leave after 3 months of an 8-month lock-in, you still owe 5 months' rent, which the landlord can deduct from your security deposit.

The landlord can deduct this substantial amount directly from your security deposit, so be certain about your plans before terminating early.
lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause provides a strong penalty if the tenant breaks the lock-in period, requiring them to pay the license fee for the remaining lock-in duration. This ensures your income and compensates for early vacancy, with the security deposit available for recovery.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: If the tenant vacates during the lock-in period (before May 31, 2027), you are entitled to collect the license fee for the entire unexpired portion of that period. You can recover this amount from their security deposit.

lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: You have the right to terminate the agreement at any time, even within the tenant's lock-in period, by giving only 15 days' written notice and without needing to state a reason. This provides you with considerable flexibility should your circumstances change.

findings.quote: After the expiry of the lock-in period, the Licensee may terminate this Agreement by giving to the Licensor not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice.

findings.quote: If the Licensee fails to hand over vacant possession of the Licensed Premises on the expiry or earlier termination of this Agreement, the Licensee shall be liable to pay to the Licensor damages calculated at three (3) times the License Fee, on a per-day basis, for every day of such unauthorised occupation, without prejudice to the other rights and remedies of the Licensor.

lensExplanations.landlord_about_to_sign: This clause imposes a significant penalty for overstaying: three times the daily license fee for each day of unauthorized occupation. This strongly deters the tenant from holding over and protects your right to regain possession.
lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: If the tenant fails to vacate the premises on time, you are entitled to charge damages at three times the daily license fee (Rs. 3,200 per day) for every day they overstay. This provides a strong incentive for timely vacation.

This is a significant responsibility and cost, so ensure you are prepared for potential repair expenses.

lensExplanations.landlord_already_signed: The tenant is responsible for all repairs, major and minor, including plumbing, electrical, water seepage, and replacing faulty fixtures or appliances. You should ensure they perform these repairs to maintain the property's condition.
